9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the discussion is converging on the decomposition B22,app = B22,HS + B22,el with B22 = 2A2Mw, and the key practical issue is what effective radius to put into B22,HS = 4 NA Vp/Mw = 32π NA R³/3Mw.

The -7.585 mL/g at pH 5 / 15 mM is B22,app. It is the sum of a salt independent positive excluded volume term and a large attractive pH/I dependent term, so it cannot be identified with the steric limit and it certainly is not the steric term itself.

For a ~150 kDa IgG, v̄ ≈0.73 mL/g gives a dry protein volume Vp,dry = Mw v̄/NA ≈1.7-1.9×10⁻¹⁹ cm³, i.e. a dry sphere radius ~3.5-3.7 nm. The osmotic virial uses the effective excluded volume radius, not the DLS hydrodynamic radius. The hydrodynamic Rh measured by DLS/SEC is 5.0-5.3 nm for a hydrated mAb and it includes the full solvation shell, translational and rotational coupling, and the Y-shape anisotropy. The radius that enters the hard-sphere excluded volume is the hydration-corrected core radius, typically 0.5-0.8 nm smaller than Rh,hydro.

Using an effective excluded volume radius Reff ≈4.5-4.8 nm after the normal hydration correction:

Reff =4.5 nm → B22,HS ≈4.5-5.0 mL/g
Reff =4.7 nm → B22,HS ≈4.9-5.6 mL/g
Reff =5.0 nm → B22,HS ≈5.5-6.5 mL/g

i.e. ≈4.5-6.5 mL/g in the protein B22 =2A2Mw convention, central ~5-6 mL/g. That is the high-salt screened plateau that is routinely quoted for mAbs, +4 to +8 mL/g with a literature central value ~+4.5-6 mL/g.

The 7-8 mL/g numbers obtained with Rh =5.0-5.3 nm inserted directly into 32πNA R³/3Mw are an over-hydrated estimate. Hydrodynamic Rh is not the hard-sphere excluded volume radius; using it without correction overcounts Vp by ~30% and is essentially double counting the hydration water that is already in the partial specific volume. For an anisotropic Y-shaped IgG the spherical hard-sphere approximation itself is an upper bound, which pushes the realistic value down further.

A steric-only value ~9-11 mL/g would require Reff ≈6.2-6.8 nm for a 150 kDa IgG in the 2A2Mw convention, which is not consistent with DLS/SEC Rh ≈4.5-5.5 nm and with the known high-ionic-strength IgG plateau. It is the radius/convention mix-up that is being flagged when Rh and Rg are interchanged.

With a conventional hydation-corrected baseline B22,HS ≈+5-6 mL/g

B22,el(pH5,15mM) ≈ B22,meas – B22,HS ≈ -7.585 – (+5 to +6) ≈ -12 to -14 mL/g,

≈ -13 mL/g for ~+5.5 mL/g, a large net attractive electrostatic/patch contribution that overwhelms the positive excluded volume and gives the observed net -7.585 mL/g. The |B22,meas|≈7.6 mL/g is the magnitude of the repulsion being compensated, not the steric coefficient itself.

So the electrostatically screened, steric-only second virial coefficient for this mAb is the positive hard-sphere baseline, ~+4.5-6.5 mL/g, nominally ~+5-6 mL/g, ~+5.5 mL/g central with a hydration-corrected Reff≈4.7-4.9 nm. That is the I→∞ limit and the value remaining once B22,el→0. The -7.585 mL/g is B22,HS + a ~-13 to -15 mL/g attractive term at pH5/15 mM, not the steric term alone.

Operationally B22,HS ≈ 32π NA Reff³ / 3 Mw ≈ 4 NA Vp,eff / Mw. The number that matters for osmotic excluded volume is Reff, the effective hard sphere radius for volume exclusion, not the hydrodynamic Rh measured by DLS/SEC.

For a ~150 kDa IgG the dry protein radius is ~3.5-3.7 nm. DLS/SEC Rh ≈ 4.7-5.5 nm is the hydrodynamic radius that includes the full bound hydration shell and the translational friction of the anisotropic Y shape. The hydration water that is hydrodynamically coupled does not contribute in the same way to the osmotic excluded volume used in the virial. I think the discussion is converging on the decomposition B22,app = B22,HS + B22,el with B22 = 2A2Mw, and the key practical issue is what effective radius to put into B22,HS = 4 NA Vp/Mw = 32π NA R³/3Mw.

The -7.585 mL/g at pH 5 / 15 mM is B22,app. It is the sum of a salt independent positive excluded volume term and a large attractive pH/I dependent term, so it cannot be identified with the steric limit and it certainly is not the steric term itself.

For a ~150 kDa IgG, v̄ ≈0.73 mL/g gives a dry protein volume Vp,dry = Mw v̄/NA ≈1.7-1.9×10⁻¹⁹ cm³, i.e. a dry sphere radius ~3.5-3.7 nm. The osmotic virial uses the effective excluded volume radius, not the DLS hydrodynamic radius. The hydrodynamic Rh measured by DLS/SEC is 5.0-5.3 nm for a hydrated mAb and it includes the full solvation shell, translational and rotational coupling, and the Y-shape anisotropy. The radius that enters the hard-sphere excluded volume is the hydration-corrected core radius, typically 0.5-0.8 nm smaller than Rh,hydro.

Using an effective excluded volume radius Reff ≈4.5-4.8 nm after the normal hydration correction:

Reff =4.5 nm → B22,HS ≈4.5-5.0 mL/g
Reff =4.7 nm → B22,HS ≈4.9-5.6 mL/g
Reff =5.0 nm → B22,HS ≈5.5-6.5 mL/g

i.e. ≈4.5-6.5 mL/g in the protein B22 =2A2Mw convention, central ~5-6 mL/g. That is the high-salt screened plateau that is routinely quoted for mAbs, +4 to +8 mL/g with a literature central value ~+4.5-6 mL/g.

The 7-8 mL/g numbers obtained with Rh =5.0-5.3 nm inserted directly into 32πNA R³/3Mw are an over-hydrated estimate. Hydrodynamic Rh is not the hard-sphere excluded volume radius; using it without correction overcounts Vp by ~30% and is essentially double counting the hydration water that is already in the partial specific volume. For an anisotropic Y-shaped IgG the spherical hard-sphere approximation itself is an upper bound, which pushes the realistic value down further.

A steric-only value ~9-11 mL/g would require Reff ≈6.2-6.8 nm for a 150 kDa IgG in the 2A2Mw convention, which is not consistent with DLS/SEC Rh ≈4.5-5.5 nm and with the known high-ionic-strength IgG plateau. It is the radius/convention mix-up that is being flagged when Rh and Rg are interchanged.

With a conventional hydation-corrected baseline B22,HS ≈+5-6 mL/g

B22,el(pH5,15mM) ≈ B22,meas – B22,HS ≈ -7.585 – (+5 to +6) ≈ -12 to -14 mL/g,

≈ -13 mL/g for ~+5.5 mL/g, a large net attractive electrostatic/patch contribution that overwhelms the positive excluded volume and gives the observed net -7.585 mL/g. The |B22,meas|≈7.6 mL/g is the magnitude of the repulsion being compensated, not the steric coefficient itself.

So the electrostatically screened, steric-only second virial coefficient for this mAb is the positive hard-sphere baseline, ~+4.5-6.5 mL/g, nominally ~+5-6 mL/g, ~+5.5 mL/g central with a hydration-corrected Reff≈4.7-4.9 nm. That is the I→∞ limit and the value remaining once B22,el→0. The -7.585 mL/g is B22,HS + a ~-13 to -15 mL/g attractive term at pH5/15 mM, not the steric term alone.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: The -7.585 mL/g measured by Zimm/Debye at pH 5 / 15 mM NaCl is B22,app = B22,HS + B22,el in the protein convention B22 = 2 A2 Mw. It is the total apparent virial under the state point, not the steric-only limit. B22,HS >0 is the salt/pH independent hard-sphere/excluded volume term, B22,HS = lim I→∞ B22,app(I), B22,el →0, and B22,el is the pH/I dependent electrostatic/patch term which is large and attractive here.

Operationally in the protein units

B22,HS ≈ 4 NA Vp / Mw ≈ 32π NA Rh,eff³ / 3 Mw

with Mw≈150 kDa. The effective radius that enters the osmotic excluded volume is the hydration-corrected hydrodynamic radius that is actually measured in solution. For a compact mAb DLS/SEC routinely gives Rh,hyd ≈5.0–5.3 nm. That Rh already contains the bound water that is osmotically active, and it is the radius that should be used in the hard-sphere estimate. Using Rh,eff ≈5.0–5.3 nm:

Rh =5.0 nm → B22,HS ≈7.0 mL/g
Rh =5.1 nm → B22,HS ≈7.3 mL/g
Rh =5.2 nm → B22,HS ≈7.7 mL/g
Rh =5.3 nm → B22,HS ≈8.0 mL/g

i.e. a high-salt screened baseline of ~7–8 mL/g, ~7.5–7.8 mL/g for the commonly quoted Rh≈5.0–5.3 nm hydrated IgG. That is the positive repulsive reference that remains once B22,el →0 and is consistent with the high-ionic-strength IgG literature plateau of ~6–8 mL/g.

With that baseline the decomposition at pH 5/15 mM is self-consistent

B22,el ≈ B22,meas – B22,HS ≈ -7.585 – (+7.5 to +8.0) ≈ -15 to -16 mL/g

a large net attractive electrostatic/patch contribution which more than compensates the ~+7–8 mL/g excluded volume and drives the net virial to -7.585 mL/g. In magnitude |B22,meas|≈7.6 mL/g is essentially the size of the steric repulsion being cancelled at low salt, which is why the ~7–8 mL/g hard-sphere magnitude is repeatedly quoted for an IgG.

A steric-only value ~9–11 mL/g would require an effective hard-sphere radius ≳6.2–6.8 nm for a 150 kDa IgG in the 2A2Mw convention, or a mix-up between Rh and Rg and/or between the protein B22=2A2Mw convention and the polymer A2 convention. That is not consistent with measured DLS/SEC Rh≈4.7–5.5 nm for monoclonals and with the textbook IgG high-salt plateau.

The argument that hydrodynamic Rh overcounts hydration double counts the effect. Rh measured by DLS/SEC is the operationally relevant size for excluded volume in solution; the hydration shell is part of the osmotically active particle. Anisotropy of the Y shape is already absorbed in the measured Rh, and removing an additional hydration correction on top of Rh pushes the estimate below the experimentally observed high-salt plateau.

Hence for this antibody the electrostatically screened steric-only / hard-sphere second virial coefficient is positive, repulsive, and of high single-digit order, ~+7–8 mL/g, about +7.5–7.8 mL/g central for Rh≈5.0–5.3 nm, ~12–16 mL/g more positive than the -7.585 mL/g apparent value measured at pH5/15 mM. The -7.585 mL/g is B22,HS + B22,el at the state point, not the steric term itself.

The -7.585 mL g-1 Zimm/Debye number at pH 5 / 15 mM NaCl is

B22,app(pH,I)= B22,HS + B22,el(pH,I) ,   B22 = 2 A2 Mw

in the protein mass convention. It is the apparent total osmotic second virial at the state point.

B22,HS >0 is the salt/pH independent hard sphere / excluded volume / purely steric part

B22,HS = limI→∞ B22,app(I) ,  B22,el →0

and B22,el(pH,I) is the pH/I dependent electrostatic/patch/depletion part. At 15 mM κ-1≈2.5 nm B22,el is large and attractive so that

B22,app = -7.585 = B22,HS + B22,el <0

is the sum of a small positive excluded volume repulsion and a large negative electrostatic/patch term. The steric term cannot be read off the single low-salt point and it is not -7.585 mL g-1. In sign the steric-only coefficient is repulsive, B22,HS>0.

Operationally

B22,HS ≃ 4 NA Vp / Mw ≃ 32π NA Reff³ /3 Mw

in the B22 =2A2Mw mL g-1 convention. For a ~150 kDa IgG v̄≈0.73 mL g-1

B22,HS ≈ +4 to +9 mL g-1

in protein units. The high-salt screened plateau that is routinely quoted for a monoclonal IgG is

B22,HS ≈ +4 to +8 mL g-1, typically ~+5–6 mL g-1, ≈+4.5–6.0 mL g-1 in the classic high ionic strength mAb literature.

With a hydration corrected effective excluded-volume radius Reff≈4.5–5.0 nm

Reff =4.5 nm → B22,HS ≈4.0–5.0 mL g-1
Reff =4.8 nm → B22,HS ≈5.4–6.0 mL g-1
Reff =5.0 nm → B22,HS ≈5.5–6.5 mL g-1

i.e. ~+4.5–6.5 mL g-1, central ~+5–6 mL g-1, ~+6 mL g-1 in round numbers, the positive salt independent excluded volume baseline that remains when B22,el→0.

If the full hydrodynamic radius reported by DLS/SEC, Rh≈5.0–5.3 nm, is inserted directly without a hydration correction the spherical hard sphere estimate becomes

Rh=5.0 nm → B22,HS≈7.0 mL g-1
Rh=5.2 nm → B22,HS≈7.7 mL g-1
Rh=5.3 nm → B22,HS≈8.0 mL g-1

i.e. the often quoted high single digit ~+7–8 mL g-1, ~+7.5–7.8 mL g-1 upper hydrated bound for this antibody. Hydrodynamic Rh already contains the full bound hydration shell and is 0.3–0.8 nm larger than the effective osmotic excluded volume radius; using it without correction overcounts Vp,eff for the anisotropic Y-shaped IgG.

With a conventional hydration-corrected baseline

B22,el(pH5,15mM)≈ B22,meas – B22,HS ≈ -7.585 – [+5 to +6] ≈ -12 to -14 mL g-1

≈ -13 to -14 mL g-1 for the customary ~+6 mL g-1 IgG estimate, ≈ -15 to -16 mL g-1 for the +7.5–8.0 mL g-1 uncorrected hydrated estimate. That is a large net attractive electrostatic/patch contribution which overwhelms the positive excluded volume and gives the observed net B22,app = -7.585 mL g-1.

The |B22,meas|≈7.6 mL g-1 magnitude is the size of the steric repulsion being compensated at low salt, not the steric coefficient itself. The electrostatically screened steric-only / hard sphere second virial for this mAb is therefore positive and repulsive, ~+4–8 mL g-1 for an IgG, nominally ~+5–6 mL g-1, ~+6 mL g-1 central textbook with a hydration corrected Reff≈4.7–5.0 nm, and ~+7–8 mL g-1, ~+7.5 mL g-1 with the larger uncorrected hydrated Rh≈5.0–5.3 nm estimate. It is ~12–16 mL g-1 more positive than the -7.585 mL g-1 apparent value measured at pH5/15 mM.

A quantitative sample-specific B22,HS strictly requires a B22(I)→I→∞ extrapolation or an independent size/mass hard-sphere estimate; it is indeterminate from the single -7.585 mL g-1 low-salt measurement alone. The measured -7.585 mL g-1 is B22,HS + B22,el at the state point, not the steric term itself.

The -7.585 mL/g measured by Zimm/Debye at pH 5 / 15 mM NaCl is B22,app = B22,HS + B22,el in the protein convention B22 = 2 A2 Mw. It is the total apparent virial under the state point, not the steric-only limit. B22,HS >0 is the salt/pH independent hard-sphere/excluded volume term, B22,HS = lim I→∞ B22,app(I), B22,el →0, and B22,el is the pH/I dependent electrostatic/patch term which is large and attractive here.

Operationally in the protein units

B22,HS ≈ 4 NA Vp / Mw ≈ 32π NA Rh,eff³ / 3 Mw

with Mw≈150 kDa. The effective radius that enters the osmotic excluded volume is the hydration-corrected hydrodynamic radius that is actually measured in solution. For a compact mAb DLS/SEC routinely gives Rh,hyd ≈5.0–5.3 nm. That Rh already contains the bound water that is osmotically active, and it is the radius that should be used in the hard-sphere estimate. Using Rh,eff ≈5.0–5.3 nm:

Rh =5.0 nm → B22,HS ≈7.0 mL/g
Rh =5.1 nm → B22,HS ≈7.3 mL/g
Rh =5.2 nm → B22,HS ≈7.7 mL/g
Rh =5.3 nm → B22,HS ≈8.0 mL/g

i.e. a high-salt screened baseline of ~7–8 mL/g, ~7.5–7.8 mL/g for the commonly quoted Rh≈5.0–5.3 nm hydrated IgG. That is the positive repulsive reference that remains once B22,el →0 and is consistent with the high-ionic-strength IgG literature plateau of ~6–8 mL/g.

With that baseline the decomposition at pH 5/15 mM is self-consistent

B22,el ≈ B22,meas – B22,HS ≈ -7.585 – (+7.5 to +8.0) ≈ -15 to -16 mL/g

a large net attractive electrostatic/patch contribution which more than compensates the ~+7–8 mL/g excluded volume and drives the net virial to -7.585 mL/g. In magnitude |B22,meas|≈7.6 mL/g is essentially the size of the steric repulsion being cancelled at low salt, which is why the ~7–8 mL/g hard-sphere magnitude is repeatedly quoted for an IgG.

A steric-only value ~9–11 mL/g would require an effective hard-sphere radius ≳6.2–6.8 nm for a 150 kDa IgG in the 2A2Mw convention, or a mix-up between Rh and Rg and/or between the protein B22=2A2Mw convention and the polymer A2 convention. That is not consistent with measured DLS/SEC Rh≈4.7–5.5 nm for monoclonals and with the textbook IgG high-salt plateau.

The argument that hydrodynamic Rh overcounts hydration double counts the effect. Rh measured by DLS/SEC is the operationally relevant size for excluded volume in solution; the hydration shell is part of the osmotically active particle. Anisotropy of the Y shape is already absorbed in the measured Rh, and removing an additional hydration correction on top of Rh pushes the estimate below the experimentally observed high-salt plateau.

B22,el is pH/I dependent and at pH 5/15 mM is large and net attractive, giving the net negative total. The –7.585 mL/g therefore cannot be identified with the steric-only term and cannot be uniquely decomposed from a single low-salt point; the steric part is repulsive.

reflection_text.11:
The measured –7.585 mL/g at pH 5 / 15 mM NaCl is B22,meas = B22,HS + B22,el in the protein B22 = 2A2Mw convention, not the steric-only limit. B22,HS >0 is the salt/pH independent hard-sphere/excluded-volume term, B22,HS = lim I→∞ B22,app, B22,el→0. B22,el is strongly pH/I dependent and at pH 5 low salt it is large and net attractive, overwhelming the positive steric repulsion to give net negative B22,meas. A single low-salt point cannot uniquely give B22,steric; a high-salt B22(I→∞) extrapolation or independent hard-sphere estimate is required.

Consensus maintained:
* Sign: B22,HS must be repulsive >0. –7.585 mL/g is B22,HS + B22,el with B22,el negative large.
* Decomposition: B22,el = B22,meas – B22,HS ≈ –7.585 – (+~5 to +8) ≈ –12 to –16 mL/g. With B22,HS≈+5–6 mL/g → B22,el≈ –12 to –14 mL/g, e.g. +6 → –13.6 mL/g. With larger Rh → B22,el≈ –15 to –16 mL/g.
* Operational formula in protein units: B22,HS ≈ 4 NA Vp/Mw = 32π NA R³/3Mw.

Ongoing disagreement is magnitude of realistic B22,HS for this IgG and what radius to use.

Colleague 1/13/5 position: use hydration-corrected hydrodynamic radius Rh≈5.0–5.3 nm directly. Then Rh=5.0 nm → ~7.0 mL/g, Rh=5.2 nm → ~7.7 mL/g, Rh=5.3 nm → ~8.0 mL/g. They identify |B22,meas|≈7.6 mL/g as the order of the steric repulsion being compensated and quote steric-only ~+7–8 mL/g, ~7.5–7.8 mL/g central. Values ~9–11 mL/g would need Rh≈6.2–6.8 nm for 150 kDa, inconsistent with measured Rh≈4.5–5.5 nm.

With realistic effective excluded-volume radius after hydration correction Rh,eff≈4.5–5.0 nm, ~4.5–6.5 mL/g central ~5–6 mL/g. They argue using DLS Rh directly overcounts hydration; Rh includes full hydration shell and is 0.3–0.8 nm larger than the effective excluded-volume radius used in B22,HS. A value ~9–11 mL/g would need Rh≈6.2–6.8 nm for 150 kDa, inconsistent with measured Rh≈4.5–5.5 nm.

* Sign convention confusion: B22,HS>0, not –7.585.
* Convention/radius confusion: 32π vs 16π, dry vs hydrated radius, B22=2A2Mw vs A2, factor ~1.5 spread.

At pH 5, 15 mM κ⁻¹≈2.5 nm, Z_eff≈15-20, B22,el is large and attractive so B22,app = -7.585 = B22,HS + B22,el <0 is the sum of a positive steric repulsion and a large negative electrostatic/patch contribution. The steric-only term cannot be read off the single low-salt point and is not -7.585 mL/g.
